articles.title: The smallest hiking cycle the Fed has ever done is 137 basis points
articles.expand: Welcome to the new rate-hike cycle. The FOMC delivered on the market's expectation for a rate hike yesterday and moved the Fed funds range to 3.75-4.00% from 3.50-3.75%. A hawkish Q A from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh left the market thinking there's an even chance of a second hike in October but there are still plenty of doves out there, who think inflation is transitory and will be quickly defeated. articles.title: Bank Of England Holds Rate Steady At 3.75%
articles.expand: The Bank of England left its key interest rate unchanged on Thursday amid limited evidence of second-round effects but further increase in energy prices raises the prospect of a hike in November. The move was in line with economists' expectations.

articles.title: The Riksbank’s Business Survey: “There was some concern before the summer, but then things took a turn for the better”
articles.expand: The economic situation has improved since last spring and, for the first time since September 2022, large Swedish companies’ assessment of the situation is now above its historical average. Before the summer, there were fears that the war in the Middle East would delay the recovery, but those fears have not materialised. Demand has strengthened and the cost increases resulting from the war are considered to be manageable. As a result, companies are taking a more optimistic view of future developments. This is revealed by the Riksbank’s Business Survey in August.
